title: Microsoft Purview: sensitivity label setting now blocks all connected experiences that analyse content in Word, Excel and PowerPoint
summary: The briefing passes: the label command, default, client versions and roadmap facts are supported. Two minor clarifications remain: the licensing source contains conflicting statements, and Microsoft links to a broader list of connected experiences than the open question suggests.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The existing Prevent some connected experiences label setting now blocks all Microsoft connected experiences for analysis of files in Word, Excel and PowerPoint rather than a subset.
claims.quote: In Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, the ‘Prevent some connected experiences that analyze content’ label setting now prevents files in these apps from being sent to all Microsoft connected experiences for analysis, rather than a subset of these connected experiences.

claims.claim: This setting has no Microsoft Purview portal configuration.
claims.quote: This configuration isn't available in the Microsoft Purview portal. You must use the PowerShell advanced setting BlockContentAnalysisServices

claims.claim: Set-Label -Identity <label name or GUID> -AdvancedSettings @{BlockContentAnalysisServices="True"} sets the label's analysis block in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: Example: Set-Label -Identity Confidential -AdvancedSettings @{BlockContentAnalysisServices="True"}

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Security & identity; Governance controls

claims.quote: you want to prevent all documents and emails with this label in Office apps from being sent to Microsoft connected experiences for analysis

claims.where: controls[0].note; Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Using Set-Label in Security & Compliance PowerShell requires assigned permissions.
claims.quote: To use this cmdlet in Security & Compliance PowerShell, you need to be assigned permissions.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; controls[0].note; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The block is admin-opt-in: BlockContentAnalysisServices defaults to False and must be configured to True to prevent analysis.
claims.quote: BlockContentAnalysisServices: Specifies a privacy setting to allow or prevent content in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook from being sent to Microsoft for content analysis. Available values are True, and False (the default).

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Removing the setting or setting it to False restores the default of sending labelled content for analysis.
claims.quote: To return the setting back to the default of sending the labeled content to Microsoft connected experiences for analysis, remove the setting or set the value to False.

claims.claim: No separate licence or plan entry specific to BlockContentAnalysisServices is published.
claims.quote: Searched: BlockContentAnalysisServices licensing sensitivity label; BlockContentAnalysisServices license pricing billing meter. Read Office apps, Set-Label, Purview service description and Get started with sensitivity labels search excerpt; no setting-specific licence entry.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft documents no separate meter for this label setting.
claims.quote: Searched: BlockContentAnalysisServices license pricing billing meter; BlockContentAnalysisServices licensing sensitivity label. Read Office apps, Set-Label, Purview service description and Get started with sensitivity labels excerpt; no meter for this Office label setting.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated that this change affects content without a label configured with the setting.
claims.quote: Searched: BlockContentAnalysisServices tenant-wide portal policy unlabeled default. Read roadmap description, Office apps control section and Set-Label default: documented reach is content with the configured label; no new effect on unlabelled or unconfigured labels stated.

claims.claim: Learn describes no new autonomous action introduced by this setting change.
claims.quote: Searched: BlockContentAnalysisServices autonomous actions default content analysis. Read roadmap description and Office apps Prevent connected experiences section: the change blocks analysis services; no new autonomous action described.

claims.claim: The documented configuration here is per label, not a tenant-wide switch for BlockContentAnalysisServices.
claims.quote: Searched: BlockContentAnalysisServices tenant-wide portal policy unlabeled default. Read Office apps, Set-Label and Connected experiences in Office; no tenant-wide form of this label advanced setting found. General Office privacy policies are distinct controls.

claims.claim: The Office apps page gives a subset table for older Windows versions rather than enumerating the broader behaviour's experiences there.
claims.quote: On newer Windows clients and on all supported MacOS and mobile client versions, the setting affects all connected experiences that analyze content in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
claims.fix: Replace the first Open questions bullet with: 'Which experiences in Microsoft's linked Connected experiences in Office list are affected on each supported client? The Office apps page links to that list and separately enumerates the older Windows subset.' Link 'Connected experiences in Office' to https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/privacy/connected-experiences and add that source.

claims.claim: The roadmap names Word, Excel and PowerPoint, while the Office apps documentation also mentions Outlook in the control paragraph.
claims.quote: The setting lets you prevent content in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook (for Prevent all connected experiences that analyze content) from being sent to Microsoft for content analysis as a privacy control.
